definition: -lalia is a historical word element from Greek meaning prattle or speech, used in terms describing forms of speaking. In the packet, it appears in echolalia, referring to repeated spoken words.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Echolalia (also Echophasia); pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports Greek lalia as “prattle,” but not the added gloss “speech.”
The statement that -lalia is “used in terms describing forms of speaking” is too general; the packet only shows it in echolalia.
The example description should stay within the packet’s wording: echolalia is the repetition of words and tones addressed to the subject, not a broader claim about repeated spoken words in general.
The packet supports that “lalia” (in the etymology of *echolalia*) means “prattle” (shown as “[Gr. … + lalia, prattle]”), but it does not support the expanded meaning “prattle or speech.”

The packet does not support the claim that “it is used in terms describing forms of speaking” in general; it only explicitly provides the element’s use in the single term *echolalia* (and *echophasia*).
